question: The base of a right prism is a regular hexagon with a side length of 8 cm. The height of the prism is 15 cm. Find the volume of the prism.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a right prism = Base Area × Height

Base Area (Regular Hexagon) = 3√3/2 × side²

Base Area = 3√3/2 × 8² = 96√3 cm²

Volume = 96√3 × 15 = 1440√3 cm³

Using √3 ≈ 1.732, Volume ≈ 1440 × 1.732 = 2494.08 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2494 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the regular hexagon base (a) = 8 cm

Height of the right prism (h) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Prism = Area of Base × Height

Area of a Regular Hexagon = [3√3 / 2] × a²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/050433b6bebca42bcdcaeb4290aee8938454b1e015456b62b9d0051d8488f7f1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the hexagonal base = [3 × 1.732 / 2] × 8²

⇒ Area of the hexagonal base = 1.5 × 1.732 × 64

⇒ Area of the hexagonal base = 2.598 × 64 = 166.272 cm²

⇒ Volume of the prism = Base Area × Height

⇒ Volume = 166.272 × 15

⇒ Volume = 2494.08 cm³

⇒ Volume ≈ 2494 cm³

**&there4$ The correct answer is 2494 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Lateral Surface Area of a Prism

LSA = Perimeter of the base × Height of the prism.

Total Surface Area of a Prism

TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Area of the base.

Regular Hexagon Area

A regular hexagon is made of 6 equilateral triangles. Area = 6 × (√3/4 × side²) = 3√3/2 × side².</p
